metaTitle: Light Vehicle Mechanic RPL: Cert III Fast Track (AUR30620)
metaDescription: Working as a mechanic without the trade papers? Fast track your AUR30620 Cert III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology with RPL. Free check.
heroIntro: The AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology is the trade qualification for car mechanics. If you've been servicing, diagnosing and repairing cars for years, RPL turns that experience into your trade certificate without an apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Mechanics who learned on the job without finishing an apprenticeship
  • Service technicians at dealerships, fleets and independent workshops
  • Workshop owners who need the trade qualification
  • Overseas-trained mechanics

Candidates usually have several years of light vehicle work across servicing, engine, brakes, steering and suspension, transmission and electrical diagnosis.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of you servicing, diagnosing and repairing vehicles
  • Job cards or repair orders you've completed
  • A reference from a qualified mechanic or workshop manager
  • Payslips, a statement of service or ABN records
  • Any certificates you hold (air conditioning, LPG, hybrid or EV safety)
  • Overseas trade certificates, translated if needed

A practical assessment, in your workshop or by video, is usually part of the process.
licensingInfo: Most states don't license individual mechanics, but some regulate repairers. For example, NSW Fair Trading issues motor vehicle repairer licences and tradesperson certificates, and in Western Australia repairers must be certified with the motor vehicle repair industry authority. A Certificate III is the qualification these schemes look for. Handling vehicle air conditioning refrigerant also needs an ARC licence.
description: The AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology covers servicing, diagnosing and repairing cars, four-wheel drives and light commercial vehicles: engines, fuel and emission systems, brakes, steering and suspension, transmissions and driveline, and electrical systems.
imageAlt: Mechanic diagnosing a car engine in a workshop

faqs.q: Can I get my mechanic's trade certificate through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have enough light vehicle experience. Your evidence, such as job cards, photos, a reference and a practical assessment, is assessed against the AUR30620 units.
Usually 6 to 12 weeks.
Your evidence and interview are online. A practical assessment is usually needed, in your workshop or by video.
It depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL usually costs far less than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.
Yes. Overseas mechanical experience is assessed against the same national units.

metaTitle: Heavy Diesel Mechanic RPL: Cert III Fast Track (AUR31120)
metaDescription: Diesel or truck mechanic? Fast track your AUR31120 Cert III in Heavy Commercial Vehicle Mechanical Technology with RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The AUR31120 Certificate III in Heavy Commercial Vehicle Mechanical Technology is the trade qualification for truck, bus and heavy vehicle mechanics. Through RPL, your years in the workshop are assessed so you can get qualified without an apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Heavy vehicle and diesel mechanics
  • Truck, bus and trailer fleet technicians
  • Mobile service mechanics
  • Overseas-trained heavy vehicle mechanics

Candidates usually have several years of heavy vehicle work including diesel engines, air brakes, transmissions, suspension and electrical systems.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of heavy vehicle servicing and repairs
  • Job cards and service records
  • A reference from a qualified mechanic or fleet manager
  • Payslips or a statement of service
  • Overseas trade certificates
licensingInfo: Heavy vehicle mechanics generally don't need a licence, though some states regulate repair businesses (for example NSW motor vehicle repairer licences). Heavy vehicle inspections for roadworthiness may need separate authorisation from your state transport authority.
description: The AUR31120 Certificate III in Heavy Commercial Vehicle Mechanical Technology covers servicing, diagnosing and repairing heavy vehicles such as trucks, buses and prime movers: diesel engines, air brake systems, transmissions, suspension, steering and electrical systems.
imageAlt: Heavy vehicle mechanic working on a truck engine

faqs.q: Can I get a heavy vehicle mechanic qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have heavy vehicle experience. Your evidence is assessed against the AUR31120 units, with a practical assessment.
Usually 6 to 12 weeks.

faqs.q: Is this the same as a diesel engine qualification?
faqs.a: No. This covers the whole heavy vehicle. If you mainly work on diesel engines, see the AUR31520 Certificate III in Automotive Diesel Engine Technology.
It depends on your evidence. Start with a free eligibility check.
